sections.title: Delivery (interactive PR lane; see $KIT/context/delivery.md)
comment: `python3 "$KIT/scripts/pr_prepare.py" prepare` validates the work and prints the exact commands.
Below git_autonomy: branch+commit+push the human runs them; at that tier the main session may push its
feature branch itself (never a protected branch; subagents never push). Merging stays the human's (IMP-25).

keys.name: delivery
doc: local | push-branch | draft-pr   (report R5, DEC-1). How finished work leaves the machine.
local       = the human merges the feature branch into the local main; nothing is pushed
(the default when the key is absent)
push-branch = the feature branch is pushed (by the main session at git_autonomy: branch+commit+push, else by you)
draft-pr    = push-branch plus `gh pr create --draft --body-file ...` (the same rule for who runs it)
The starter config /chain-of-custody:init writes sets push-branch (with git_autonomy: branch+commit+push):
the main session pushes its own feature branch and you open the PR.
Merging is always the human's act. The doctor suggests draft-pr once the ruleset checks pass.
branch, verify, then pr_prepare prints the push and draft-PR commands for me to run

keys.name: git_autonomy
doc: none | branch | branch+commit | branch+commit+push   (DEC-22). What the main session may do with git itself.
none          = it asks you to create the branch and to commit (v1 behaviour; the default when the key is absent)
branch        = it creates and switches to `feat/<slug>` itself
branch+commit = it also makes one WIP commit per engineer so reviewers see `prev..sha`
branch+commit+push = it also pushes its feature branch (`git push <remote> feat/<slug>`, no force, never a
protected branch) and, with delivery: draft-pr, opens the draft PR. Needs delivery push-branch or
draft-pr, and counts only once this value is committed on the base branch. The starter config
/chain-of-custody:init writes sets this tier: the main session pushes its own feature branch
Subagents never push. Merge, rebase, force-push and `gh pr merge` stay yours at every setting.
the conductor branches and makes the WIP commits; I push

keys.name: max_ci_fix_attempts
doc: CI-fix commits allowed on one PR (report F-28). While fixing CI, edits to `.github/workflows/**`,
acceptance tests and lockfiles are refused; each fix commit carries a `CI-Fix-Of: <sha>` trailer.
Still red after the last attempt: stop and hand it to a human.
CI-fix attempts per PR

keys.name: always_human_paths
doc: Extra path globs a human must review on top of the kit's built-in list (report H3): migrations, auth,
payments, infra, .github/, .claude/, lockfiles, test and CI config, deploy files. pr_prepare lists
every changed path that matches and refuses a PR body that says "none" when the diff touches one.
- src/auth/**
- src/payments/**
project paths a human always reviews (the kit's own list always applies)

keys.name: verify_build
doc: Optional G6 stages, run by `python3 "$KIT/scripts/verify.py"` before the tests, in this order:
verify_build, verify_lint, verify_typecheck. Empty = the stage does not run (see verify_require).
production build

keys.name: verify_lint
doc: lint command; must exit 0
lint

keys.name: verify_typecheck
doc: typecheck command; must exit 0
typecheck

keys.name: verify_require
doc: Stages verify.py refuses to skip: build | lint | typecheck | tests | smoke. A required stage with no
command is a configuration error, never a silent pass. `tests` always runs when verify_tests is set.
none of these may be left unconfigured

keys.name: verify_ports
doc: Dedicated verify ports (not the dev-server defaults, L-27). Checked free before the smoke stage; a busy
port is an `env` failure, never a retry. Checked again after it: a port still bound means the dev server leaked.
With verify_dev the first port is where verify.py polls and sends the smoke requests.
web and API verify ports

keys.name: verify_dev
doc: Optional. A dev-server command that never exits. verify.py starts it in its own process group, polls
http://127.0.0.1:<first verify port><verify_ready_path> until it answers or verify_run_timeout_s passes,
requests the item's demo route, then kills the whole group. Takes the place of verify_run for the smoke stage.
Gets VERIFY_PORT (the first verify port) in its environment.

keys.name: verify_ready_path
doc: Path polled for readiness when verify_dev is set. Any status below 400 counts as ready.

keys.name: verify_timeout_s
doc: Seconds each build, lint, typecheck and test stage may run. On expiry the stage's process group is killed.
per-stage timeout (seconds)

keys.name: verify_run_timeout_s
doc: Seconds the smoke stage may run (boot, readiness, requests, teardown) before its process group is killed.
smoke-stage timeout (seconds)

keys.name: verify_env_allow
doc: Names of extra environment variables verify.py passes through. Everything else is dropped: it runs the
stages under an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, locale, toolchain locators), so no token or cloud
credential of the calling shell reaches test code. Names only; never put a value or a secret here.
extra variables the toolchain needs
